intro: The Maldives is a chain of coral islands in the Indian Ocean whose sultans ruled for over 800 years.

chapters.title: Seafarers and cowrie shells
text: Early settlers came from South Asia and were Buddhist. The islands were famous for cowrie shells, used as money across Asia and Africa.

chapters.title: The sultanate
text: In 1153 the king converted to Islam, and sultans ruled until 1968. The Portuguese held Malé briefly in the 1500s, and Britain protected the islands from 1887.

chapters.title: Independence
text: The Maldives became independent in 1965 and a republic in 1968. Tourism began in the 1970s. Democracy arrived with multi-party elections in 2008, and the 2004 tsunami hit many islands.

highlight.title: Underwater cabinet
highlight.text: In 2009 the cabinet met underwater in scuba gear to warn the world about rising seas.

keyTerms.meaning: A small shell once used as money.
